title: A Stronger Mixture of Low-Rank Experts for Fine-Tuning Foundation Models
summary: Two rank-one expert calculations disprove the Appendix E implementation-to-update equality and the general inference of closer full-gradient approximation. Original experiments not reproduced.
limitations: No author-code execution or benchmark reproduction.
No full multi-token, changing-gate, upstream-gradient or AdamW repair certified.
References pp10-12 not exhaustively checked; no comprehensive later-version/erratum search.
Optional OpenReview metadata unavailable (403); embedded appendix available.
Controller-owned conversation URL and visible-model observation not supplied.

problems.source_claim: Equation13/Algorithm1 achieves Equation12; AppendixE derives next-X using frozen detached products.
assumptions: Two activated experts, positive normalized gates 1/2.
d2,r1; A=(1,0),B=(1,0)^T for each; invertible scalar Gram matrices1.
Gate logits have zero gradient for identical outputs; deterministic local theory, not dropout benchmark trajectory.
problems.check: At next forward detached products are refreshed. Actual coefficients are g^(3/2), not g. Xnew=(1-eta/sqrt2)^2 P; Eq11 gives (1-eta)^2 P. Appendix frozen surrogate=(1-2eta+eta^2/sqrt2)P.
problems.result: A first-order difference survives eta->0; static release confirms recomputation.
problems.counterevidence: Forward values and direct gate derivative preserved; frozen local surrogate has paper coefficient but is not next model output; g=1 is valid; ridge1e-6 does not fix mismatch.
problems.core_dependency: AppendixE is the explicit justification connecting the central implementable strategy with the ideal gate-rescaled update.
problems.impact: Major core derivation; no benchmark refutation.

correction.statement: For fixed gates and simultaneous preconditioned SGD, actual first-order update is -eta sum g^(3/2)(P_i G+G Q_i).
correction.limits: Not a repaired full algorithm; shared-token and AdamW behavior need separate analysis.

problems.source_claim: Section3.2 claims Eq12 further approaches full fine-tuning, motivated by normalization of squared gate weights.
assumptions: Same fully admissible two-expert example as P1.
Same learning rate, matrix Frobenius distance to full-gradient descent direction.
No subspace-disjointness assumption in paper's argument.
problems.check: Ordinary direction G, Eq12 direction2G, actual engineering sqrt2G; errors from G are0,1,sqrt2-1. Ordinary finite update differs from FFT by O(eta^2), alternatives by O(eta).
problems.result: Scalar normalization alone does not establish closer FFT approximation; overlapping row/column projections double-count common component.
problems.counterevidence: Qualitative empirical tendency could hold; learning-rate retuning matches this one example but does not prove a general claim. No quantified benchmark performance conclusion.
problems.core_dependency: Closeness to global full fine-tuning is the central theoretical rationale for rescaling.
problems.impact: Major invalid core justification as presented; not a claim method performs poorly.

correction.statement: Specify metric, conditions and valid comparative argument.

clarifications.result: Verified under invertible Gram matrices and simultaneous plain preconditioned SGD.
